instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: Claudius became Roman emperor in AD 41. At first, people didn’t think he would be a good leader because he had a physical condition that meant he had trouble speaking and walking.
atoms.sound: Cloudius became Roman emperor in AD 41. At first, people didn’t think he would be a good leader because he had a physical condition that meant he had trouble speaking and walking.

atoms.text: In Roman society, his disability was seen as a sign of weakness, and Claudius was not expected to achieve power and success.
atoms.sound: In Roman society, his disability was seen as a sign of weakness, and Cloudius was not expected to achieve power and success.

atoms.text: However, contrary to peoples’ expectations, Emperor Claudius became a leader who changed how the empire was run and expanded it to new areas, including Britain in AD 43.
atoms.sound: However, contrary to peoples’ expectations, Emperor Cloudius became a leader who changed how the empire was run and expanded it to new areas, including Britain in AD 43.

atoms.a: Why did Romans underestimate Claudius as a leader?
atoms.sound: Why did Romans underestimate Cloudius as a leader?
b: because he had lots of enemies

atoms.a: How did Roman society view Claudius’ disability?
atoms.sound: How did Roman society view Cloudius’s disability?
b: Diversity was seen as a strength.

atoms.a: How did the empire change during Claudius’ rule?
atoms.sound: How did the empire change during Cloudius’s rule?
b: ++Emperor Claudius expanded the empire to Britain.
Roman Empire collapsed during Claudius’ rule.
Emperor Claudius was a careful leader who avoided changes.

instruction.text: Fill in the gaps in the conversation.

atoms.b: I want to be the first Roman emperor to successfully ((++conquer travel_to)) Britain.
Julius ((++Caesar Cleopatra)) invaded Britain about a hundred years ago, but he didn’t conquer it. Many believe Britain is too wild and distant to conquer.
Caesar was not prepared for the ((++weather dragons)), and he didn’t bring enough cavalry or supplies. I will not repeat his mistakes!
I will prepare carefully and bring a huge ((++army group_of_friends)). We will be ready for the fierce tribes!

hint.text: Almost everything we know about Claudius’ invasion comes from a single source: a Roman historian called Cassius Dio. He wrote about the events almost 200 years after they took place, so we probably shouldn’t believe everything he wrote!
hint.sound: Almost everything we know about Klawdeus’s invasion comes from a single source: a Roman historian called Cassius Dio. He wrote about the events almost 200 years after they took place, so we probably shouldn’t believe everything he wrote!
hint.label: Did you know?

atoms.a: It is said Emperor Claudius brought war elephants to scare the Britons.
atoms.sound: It is said Emperor Klawdeus brought war elephants to scare the Britons.
atoms.b: war elephants

atoms.a: Roman soldiers used war machines to shoot stones and iron-tipped bolts.
atoms.b: war machines

atoms.a: Emperor Claudius invaded Britain with a huge army of 40,000 soldiers.
atoms.sound: Emperor Klawdeus invaded Britain with a huge army of 40,000 soldiers.
atoms.b: huge army

finish.text: Claudius’ army was much more organised and professional than the warriors they faced in Britain.
finish.sound: Klawdeus’s army was much more organised and professional than the warriors they faced in Britain.

instruction.text: Listen and select the correct answer.

atoms.a: What do you think happened next?

b.sound: South-eastern Britain was conquered quickly as eleven Keltic tribes surrendered.
The Keltic tribes defeated the Roman army, and took over the empire.

instruction.text: Fill in the gaps to understand why Rome used client kings.

atoms.b: My people are ((++worried calm)). What will happen to us now?
That depends on you. Rome has the ((++soldiers farmers)) to take this land by force. We have ((++conquered befriended)) many tribes, and your warriors cannot stop us.
Then what choice do we have?

You can become a client king. That means you may keep being the leader, and your people are spared, but you must ((++follow break)) Roman laws, ((++obey challenge)) Roman orders and be loyal to the empire.
This way, Rome controls the region without governing it ((++directly secretly)). We do not need to station as many soldiers here if you keep order for us.
And what if I refuse?
Then you will not be king for long! If you refuse, we will ((++take_over let_you_rule)) your land by force.

feedback.finish: Many chiefs became client kings. They stayed in power by being loyal to Rome and helping the Romans govern their land, but the threat of the Roman army was always there.

atoms.a: In which two ways did client kings make ruling easier for Rome?
b: ++The Romans did not have to govern the land directly.
++Rome could control an area without sending as many soldiers.
Client kings ruled the whole Roman Empire.
